# Print the name of the shape.

cases.name: Typed 10

cases.name: Typed 2

cases.name: Typed 11

cases.name: Typed 6

shape.check:
import re
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1, "One if/elif/else chain is enough: every case is a different alternative for the same value."
assert re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "Use elif for the middle alternatives."
assert re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "End the chain with else for a count outside 3 to 10."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Store the name inside the branches, then print once after the chain."
assert __stdout__.strip().endswith("."), "End the sentence with a full stop."
hints: Store the name in the branches and print one f-string after the chain. The `else` branch stores the text for a count the chain does not know, so the same print works for every case.
shape.answerNote: The chain compares sides with each count in turn. Whatever branch runs, the single print after it finishes the sentence.

cases.name: Typed 6
cases.expected: Magnitude: A magnitude 6.0 earthquake is strong.

cases.expected: Magnitude: A magnitude 8.0 earthquake is great.

richter.check:
import re
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1, "One if/elif/else chain is enough: every case is a different alternative for the same value."
assert re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "Use elif for the middle alternatives."
assert re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "End the chain with else for 10.0 or more."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Store the descriptor inside the branches, then print once after the chain."
assert __code__.count("<") + __code__.count(">") <= 9, "Order the branches so each one needs a single comparison; the earlier branches have already ruled out the smaller magnitudes."
hints: Test the ranges from the smallest up. Once `magnitude < 2.0` has failed, the next `elif magnitude < 3.0` already knows the value is at least 2.0, so one comparison per branch is enough.
richter.answerNote: Each branch of the chain only runs after every earlier test has failed, so `elif magnitude < 3.0` covers exactly 2.0 up to but not including 3.0.

zodiac.starter:
year = int(input('Year: '))
# Print the animal for the year.

cases.name: Typed 2019
cases.expected: Year: 2019 is the year of the Pig.

cases.name: Typed 2000
cases.expected: Year: 2000 is the year of the Dragon.

cases.name: Typed 2026
cases.expected: Year: 2026 is the year of the Horse.

cases.name: Typed 1999
cases.expected: Year: 1999 is the year of the Hare.

cases.name: Typed 1925
cases.expected: Year: 1925 is the year of the Ox.

cases.name: Typed 0
cases.expected: Year: 0 is the year of the Monkey.

cases.name: Typed 2035
cases.expected: Year: 2035 is the year of the Hare.

zodiac.check:
import re
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1, "One if/elif/else chain is enough: every case is a different alternative for the same value."
assert re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "Use elif for the middle alternatives."
assert "%" in __code__, "Use % to find where the year falls in the 12-year cycle."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Store the animal inside the branches, then print once after the chain."
assert __code__.count("elif") >= 10, "The chain needs one branch per animal: eleven tests and an else."
hints: The cycle repeats every 12 years, so `year % 12` is the same for 2000, 2012 and 1988. Work out what it is for each year in the table, then write one branch per value.
`2000 % 12` is 8, so a remainder of 8 is the Dragon. `2001 % 12` is 9, the Snake, and so on up to 11, the Sheep. `2004 % 12` wraps round to 0, the Monkey.
zodiac.answerNote: 2000 % 12 is 8, so remainder 8 is the Dragon and the table wraps: 2004 gives 0 (Monkey) through 2011 giving 7 (Hare). Any year from 0 up works because % always lands in 0 to 11.

note.starter:
note = input('Note: ')
# Print the frequency of the note.

cases.name: Typed A4
cases.expected: Note: A4 has a frequency of 440.00 Hz.

cases.name: Typed C4
cases.expected: Note: C4 has a frequency of 261.63 Hz.

cases.name: Typed C5
cases.expected: Note: C5 has a frequency of 523.26 Hz.

cases.name: Typed A3
cases.expected: Note: A3 has a frequency of 220.00 Hz.

cases.name: Typed C0
cases.expected: Note: C0 has a frequency of 16.35 Hz.

cases.name: Typed B8
cases.expected: Note: B8 has a frequency of 7902.08 Hz.

cases.name: Typed G6
cases.expected: Note: G6 has a frequency of 1568.00 Hz.

note.check:
import re
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1, "One if/elif/else chain is enough: every case is a different alternative for the same value."
assert re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "Use elif for the middle alternatives."
assert __code__.count("elif") == 5 and re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "One chain with seven branches, one per letter: an if, five elifs and an else."
assert "[" in __code__, "Pick the letter and the octave digit out of note with indexes."
assert "**" in __code__, "Use ** to double or halve the fourth-octave frequency the right number of times."
assert re.search(r":[^}]*\.2f\}", __source__), "Show the frequency with two decimal places."
assert len(__stdout__.strip().splitlines()) == 1, "Print one line."
hints: `note[0]` is the letter and `int(note[1])` is the octave number. The chain only needs to know the letter: store that letter's fourth-octave frequency from the table in `base`.

Going up one octave doubles the frequency and going down one halves it. From octave 4 to octave `octave` that is `octave - 4` doublings, so the answer is `base * 2 ** (octave - 4)`. A negative exponent halves.
note.answerNote: 2 ** (octave - 4) is 1 for octave 4, 2 for octave 5, and 0.5 for octave 3, so one multiplication moves the base frequency to any octave.
